title: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Digital Development and Information)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Digital Development and Information)

sections.label: Digital economy GDP growth
sections.summary: Singapore's digital economy grew from 13% of GDP in 2017 to 17.3% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Our latest push in digitalisation has seen positive results, as our digital economy grew from contributing 13% of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2017 to 17.3% in 2022.

sections.label: Digital infrastructure resilience measures
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister what measures build up digital infrastructure and ensure its resilience and security.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: A small failure in our digital infrastructure can cause major disruptions to our economic activities and daily lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, can the Minister share what measures are being put in place to build up our digital infrastructure further and ensure its resilience and security?

sections.label: Data centres energy and sustainability
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to elaborate on balancing digital infrastructure growth with environmental sustainability commitments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Data centres, the backbone of a digital economy, currently consume around 1% to 1.5% of global electricity, a figure that Goldman Sachs Research projects will increase by 50% by 2027 and potentially by up to 165% by 2030 compared to 2023 levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, as we embrace digitalisation, we must also accelerate our decarbonisation efforts, enhance energy security and reduce reliance on brown energy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, can the Minister elaborate on the Government's strategy to balance the growth of our digital infrastructure with our commitment to environmental sustainability?

sections.label: Update on online harms motion
sections.summary: The passage asks for an update since the January 2024 Motion and notes online harms and support centre approaches have doubled.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Could the Minister give an update on what has transpired or implemented since the Motion with these 13 calls to action in January 2024?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In the very recent media report, we have been told that, and that is just last month, that online harms have been increasing because the number of people who have been approaching support centres to received help for online harms have pretty much doubled.

sections.label: Motion calls and harmful behaviour legislation
sections.summary: The passage asks the Government to focus on 13 calls for action and consider legislation against cybercrimes, scams and bullying.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Last year, the GPC tabled a Motion in Parliament, in which we put forward 13 calls for action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can focus on these 13 calls and continue to enhance the overall safety of our digital society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In addition, can we also consider legislation to strengthen the crackdown on harmful behaviours, such as cybercrimes, scams and bullying?

sections.label: National AI Strategy 2.0 outcomes
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for efforts and outcomes in driving AI adoption, experimentation and innovation since NAIS 2.0 launched in December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Narrowing the focus on AI, Singapore has a clear strategy as set out in the National AI Strategy (NAIS) 2.0 report.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: In the report, Singapore sees AI as no longer an opportunity but a necessity, that it has to go from projects to system and that it has to go from local to global.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Now that NAIS 2.0 has been launched for more than a year since December 2023, can the Minister share what are some of the efforts and outcomes in driving adoption, experimentation and innovation for the Government and industry?

sections.label: Industry Digital Plans refresh
sections.summary: The passage asks how refreshed and new Industry Digital Plans for several sectors address sector-specific AI tools and challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: With the recent refresh of the Industry Digital Plans (IDPs) for several sectors and the launch of new IDPs for the legal and tourism sectors, can the Minister elaborate on how these plans are tailored to address sector-specific AI tools and challenges?

sections.label: Digital Economy Agreements collaboration
sections.summary: The passage asks for an update on Singapore's global collaboration on capabilities, data sharing and online harms, and notes SPH Media Trust missed some KPIs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: In a world where digital economies are increasingly interconnected, Singapore's role as a financial and trade hub is more important than ever.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: We have signed Digital Economy Agreements (DEAs) with countries, such as Australia, the United Kingdom (UK) and New Zealand, and we are actively advancing the Association for Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Digital Economy Framework Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: These initiatives will facilitate data sharing, harmonise understanding and standards, promote technological collaboration and perhaps also help combat online harms, ensuring that we remain at the forefront of the global digital economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Therefore, can the Minister provide an update on how the Government is collaborating with governments and organisations globally to build capabilities, facilitate data sharing and transactions, and combat online harms?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister said that while SPH Media Trust had maintained its overall reach and achieved a modest increase in its digital subscriptions, it did not meet all its KPIs on digital reach, youth reach, vernacular reach and average time spent on its websites and apps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Accordingly, it did not receive the full funding that was committed.

sections.label: BBC job cuts
sections.summary: The passage states BBC announced plans in July 2024 to cut 500 jobs by March next year to save £200 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In July 2024, BBC announced plans to cut 500 jobs by March next year in a bid to save £200 million and become a "leaner, more agile organisation", as it copes with funding and inflationary pressures.

sections.label: SPH Media layoffs
sections.summary: The passage states SPH Media announced in November last year it laid off 34 employees, 10% of its technology division.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Back home, SPH Media announced in November last year that it has laid off 34 employees, amounting to 10% of its technology division amidst its restructuring and digital transformation.

sections.label: DigitalAccess@Home household numbers
sections.summary: The passage asks how many households have benefited from DigitalAccess@Home to date.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For example, how many households have benefited from DigitalAccess@Home to date?

sections.label: Digital for Life collaboration
sections.summary: The passage states IMDA announced a strategic collaboration with over 300 partners under the National Digital for Life Movement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: IMDA announced a strategic collaboration involving over 300 partners under the National Digital for Life Movement to help advance Singaporeans' essential digital skills.

sections.label: Walk-in computer stations for agencies
sections.summary: All agencies should have walk-in computer stations staffed by officers trained in that agency's processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Instead, all agencies should have walk-in computer stations staffed by officers who are trained in that agency's processes.

sections.label: ServiceSG expansion and Seniors Go Digital
sections.summary: The ServiceSG network should be expanded, including to Serangoon, and Seniors Go Digital was introduced to help older Singaporeans navigate digital services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The ServiceSG network should also be expanded, including to Serangoon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Seniors Go Digital programme was introduced to help older Singaporeans navigate digital services.

sections.label: Public results for public funds
sections.summary: If public funds are being used, the results should be made public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If public funds are being used, the results should be made public.

sections.label: IMDA mystery shopper test findings
sections.summary: IMDA's mystery shopper test showed Instagram acted on 2% of legitimate reports, Facebook averaged nine days and X ten days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: IMDA's mystery shopper test showed that Instagram acted on just 2% of legitimate user reports on content that violated its own community guidelines in the first instance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Facebook took an average of nine days to act on legitimate user reports, and X took an average of 10 days, much, much longer than the median time of 15.06 hours – very precise, I must add – that X itself has declared in its annual report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Taken together, most of these designated social media services took action on only around half of legitimate user reports and took an average of five days to act.

sections.label: IMDA fines and Telegram designation
sections.summary: The passage asks how many fines IMDA has imposed on platforms and whether there are plans to designate Telegram as a social media service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: How many fines has IMDA imposed so far on the platforms for failing to fulfil their obligations under our laws?

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And three, are there plans to finally designate Telegram as a social media service, too, because, in practice, it is a social media service, not just a messaging app?

sections.label: Checking seniors' eligibility details
sections.summary: Anyone can check a senior's Retirement Account sum, monthly earnings and residence annual value using their NRIC number and date of birth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Anyone can check whether a senior has less than the Basic Retirement Sum in their Retirement Account, earns less than $4,000 a month, and if the annual value of their residence is below $21,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: All this information can be unlocked with a senior's NRIC number and date of birth.

sections.label: Enterprise Compute Initiative eligibility
sections.summary: The $150 million Enterprise Compute Initiative announced in Budget 2025 aims to address business challenges in adopting AI solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The new Enterprise Compute Initiative of $150 million announced in Budget 2025 aims to address these challenges that businesses face in adopting AI solution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: How can businesses tap the Enterprise Compute Initiative and what are the eligibility criteria to qualify?

sections.label: National AI Strategy 2.0
sections.summary: The latest iteration of the National AI Strategy 2.0 was launched in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The latest iteration of the National AI Strategy (NAIS) 2.0 was launched in 2023.

sections.label: DBS AI job cuts
sections.summary: DBS Group announced it will cut 4,000 jobs over the next three years, highlighting AI's growing impact.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: DBS Group's recent announcement to cut 4,000 jobs over the next three years highlights AI's growing impact.

sections.label: AI workforce transition support
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Government is preparing businesses and workers, especially SMEs and vulnerable roles, for AI.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: As AI reshapes the job landscape, how is the Government ensuring that businesses and the workers, especially in SMEs and vulnerable roles are prepared?

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: What initiatives are in place to help the Workforce develop AI skills for productivity gains and how will workers in these sectors be supported through this transition?

sections.label: AI productivity gains limits
sections.summary: Many enterprises use AI tools like Microsoft Co-Pilot, but these typically deliver only 10% to 20% productivity improvement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Many enterprises are already using AI to drive productivity, especially individual productivity, deploying tools like Microsoft Co-Pilot – but these productivity-driven AI use cases typically deliver only 10% to 20% productivity improvement.

sections.label: Supporting local AI adoption
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry supports local enterprises to accelerate AI adoption for larger scale value creation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How is the Ministry supporting our local enterprises to accelerate the adoption of AI for larger scale value creation, so that Singapore can continue to harness AI for economic gains and social benefit?

sections.label: TeSA and AI practitioner target
sections.summary: Asks how effective TeSA has been in equipping the local workforce with deep tech skills for AI and cybersecurity roles, and whether the AI practitioner target is on track.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On developing expert capabilities, how effective has a TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) been in equipping our local workforce with the deep tech skills needed for AI and cybersecurity roles?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Are we on track to meet our target for AI practitioners?

sections.label: Budget 2024 AI industry collaborations
sections.summary: States that Budget 2024 announced collaborations with industry to drive AI adoption and innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In Budget 2024, it was announced that there would be collaborations with industry to drive AI adoption and innovation.

sections.label: NAIS 2.0 strategy progress
sections.summary: Asks how Singapore is progressing in its NAIS 2.0 strategy to realise its vision of AI as a force for good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: How are we progressing in our NAIS 2.0 strategy to realise Singapore's vision of AI as a force for good, one that empowers businesses and uplifts our people?

sections.label: Raising national cybersecurity posture
sections.summary: Notes rising cybersecurity threats and the amended Cybersecurity Act, and asks how the national cybersecurity posture will continue to be raised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Cybersecurity threats continue to be on the rise, while we have amended our Cybersecurity Act to strengthen the protection of critical information infrastructures and expand the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore's (CSA's) oversight to cover new classes, how do we continue to raise our national cybersecurity posture?

sections.label: Microsoft and IMDA AI training
sections.summary: States Microsoft partnered with NTUC Learning Hub to train up to 100,000 workers in AI skills, and IMDA is working with SkillsFuture Singapore to expand SkillsFuture for Digital Workplace 2.0.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, Microsoft has partnered with NTUC Learning Hub to train up to 100,000 workers with AI skills.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: At the same time, IMDA is working with SkillsFuture Singapore to expand the curriculum in SkillsFuture for Digital Workplace 2.0 to include AI and Gen AI content.

sections.label: Expanding AI practitioner pool
sections.summary: Updates that the AI practitioner pool grew by nearly 25% in the last year, towards the ambition of expanding from under 5,000 to 15,000 in about five years.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In response to Mr Sharael Taha and Ms Tin Pei Ling, let me provide an update on efforts to expand our pool of AI practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I previously shared our ambition to expand the pool from under 5,000 to 15,000 in about five years.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the last year or so, we estimate that the pool has grown by nearly 25%.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) is on track to hire and train a 300-person AI workforce by end-2025.

sections.label: Age assurance for social media
sections.summary: MDDI is studying whether age assurance obligations for app stores should also apply to social media services, as measures to protect children from harmful content are unsatisfactory.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Their measures to protect children from harmful content are also far from satisfactory.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is why MDDI is studying whether the age assurance obligations for app stores should also apply to social media services.

sections.label: Online Safety Commission Bill
sections.summary: The Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Bill will be introduced later this year and will establish the Online Safety Commission by the first half of 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: During the Smart Nation 2.0 launch, the Prime Minister announced that the Government will introduce new legislation to support victims seeking relief from specified online harms.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Ms Tin will be glad to know that the proposed law, the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Bill, will be introduced later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It will establish a new agency called the Online Safety Commission (OSC) so that victims can get timely help if they encounter online harms.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The OSC will be set up by the first half of 2026.

sections.label: Digital Infrastructure Act planned
sections.summary: The amendments are expected to come into force later this year, and a new Digital Infrastructure Act is to be introduced to enhance security and resilience of digital infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The amendments are expected to come into force later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Beyond cybersecurity, we aim to introduce a new Digital Infrastructure Act to enhance security and resilience of digital infrastructure.

sections.label: Cyber marks for vendors
sections.summary: Possible measures include requiring vendors and their subcontractors to obtain Cyber Essentials or Cyber Trust Marks before licensing or bidding for Government contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Possible measures include requiring these vendors and their subcontractors to obtain their Cyber Essentials or Cyber Trust Marks before they can be licensed or bid for contracts offered by the Government.

sections.label: Elections online advertising amendment
sections.summary: The Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising) (Amendment) Act was passed to protect Singaporeans from AI-generated misinformation during elections.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We share the same concern as Members that AI-enabled tools, like deepfakes, may be abused to cause harm.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is why we passed the Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising) (Amendment) Act to protect Singaporeans from the threat of AI-generated misinformation during elections.

sections.label: SPH Media digital subscriptions
sections.summary: SPH Media's digital subscriptions have held steady and are now 35% higher than print subscriptions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Without revealing commercially sensitive information, I can share that SPH Media's digital subscriptions have held steady and it is now 35% higher than print subscriptions.

sections.label: PSM prominence rules study
sections.summary: MDDI is studying other countries' rules requiring Connected TVs to pre-load and prominently display public service media apps, and will consult industry before deciding next steps.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Countries like the UK and Australia have, therefore, made new rules.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: They now require Connected TVs to be pre-loaded with public service media apps like BBC iPlayer, or ABC iview, and to display these apps prominently on their user interfaces.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Our PSM content must remain visible and easily accessible to our audiences.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Therefore, MDDI is studying the regulatory moves in other countries to safeguard the prominence and discoverability of PSM.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will consult industry stakeholders, including device manufacturers, before deciding the next steps.

sections.label: PSM accessibility for Singaporeans
sections.summary: The Government is exploring ways to make Public Service Media content more accessible to Singaporeans in the new media environment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Only they will report news and analyse international events and their impact on us from Singapore's perspective.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Therefore, the Government is exploring ways to make Public Service Media content more accessible to Singaporeans in the new media environment.

sections.label: Digital Infrastructure Act resilience
sections.summary: A new Digital Infrastructure Act is planned this year to improve digital resilience and security, targeting major cloud service providers and data centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We cannot eliminate risk completely, so we must enhance our preparedness by reducing the occurrence and the impact of disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are working towards introducing a new law this year, called the Digital Infrastructure Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This will improve Singapore's digital resilience and security.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The Act targets foundational digital infrastructure, starting with major cloud service providers and data centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The Act will require major operators to implement measures to uphold their resilience and security and to minimise disruptions.

sections.label: Service availability increase
sections.summary: Service availability for these systems rose from 95% to 99.5% in the last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Service availability for these systems rose from 95% to 99.5% in the last year.

sections.label: 10GB plan price drop
sections.summary: A 10GB plan now costs between $30 and $70, compared to more than $100 a year ago.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: A 10GB plan now costs between $30 and $70, compared to more than $100 a year ago.

sections.label: Green Data Centre Roadmap
sections.summary: IMDA launched the Green Data Centre Roadmap last year to guide data centres to improve energy efficiency and use green energy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: IMDA launched the Green Data Centre Roadmap last year to guide data centres to improve energy efficiency and use green energy to grow AI compute capacity sustainably.

sections.label: Pair Chat Gen AI assistant
sections.summary: Pair Chat is a fast and secure Gen AI assistant used by more than half the Public Service today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Pair Chat is a fast and secure Gen AI assistant used by more than half the Public Service today.

sections.label: Litmus launch with IMDA
sections.summary: Litmus is built in partnership with IMDA's Moonshot and will be launched this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Litmus is built in partnership with IMDA's Moonshot and will be launched this year.

sections.label: Sentinel AI guardrails platform
sections.summary: Guardrails keep AI systems within ethical, legal and functional boundaries, and the Government is building Sentinel to provide guardrails as a service.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In the AI world, guardrails ensure that AI systems operate within ethical, legal and functional boundaries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are building Sentinel, a platform that provides guardrails as a service for the Government's AI applications.

sections.label: Digital economy growth rate
sections.summary: The digital economy grew at a compound annual growth rate of 11.2% from 2018 to 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The digital economy has grown at a compound annual growth rate of 11.2% from 2018 to 2023.

sections.label: SMEs Go Digital Programme outcomes
sections.summary: Initiatives such as the SMEs Go Digital Programme helped about 100,000 SMEs since 2017, with rising digital adoption and reported cost savings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Through initiatives, such as the SMEs Go Digital Programme, we have helped about 100,000 SMEs since 2017, with 40,000 SMEs benefiting over the last four years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The share of SMEs adopting at least one digital solution for general business functions increased from 53% in 2020 to 84% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: On average, SMEs that adopted digital solutions under the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) between 2018 and 2023, reported cost savings of 48% per solution.

sections.label: CTO-as-a-Service platform usage
sections.summary: In 2024, over 330,000 users accessed the CTO-as-a-Service platform, which helped almost 3,000 SMEs adopt AI-enabled solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: In 2024, over 330,000 users accessed resources on the Chief Technology Officer (CTO)-as-a-Service platform, which helped almost 3,000 SMEs adopt AI-enabled solutions.

sections.label: iHub AI report tool
sections.summary: iHub employees can create reports automatically with simple prompts, halving report time, and customers can derive real-time supply chain insights.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: With this tool, iHub's employees can create reports automatically using simple prompts, reducing the time spent on these reports by half. iHub's customers can also use it to derive real-time supply chain insights to inform their decisions.

sections.label: IMDA Gen AI Playbook
sections.summary: IMDA will launch a Gen AI Playbook for Enterprises catering to different stages of digital maturity, building on early adopters' experience.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Building on the experience and best practices of early adopters, IMDA will launch a Gen AI Playbook for Enterprises catering to different stages of their digital maturity.

sections.label: Gen AI Navigator tool
sections.summary: IMDA will launch the Gen AI Navigator, an online tool recommending Gen AI solutions, grant-supported solutions and SSG-funded training, available on the CTO-as-a-Service platform.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: So, the Playbook has something for all enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: And complementing the Playbook, IMDA will launch an online tool, the Gen AI Navigator, that recommends the right Gen AI solution for specific business needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The Navigator will also point to solutions with grant support and SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG)-funded training that can help SMEs understand how to leverage Gen AI for growth.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: These tools will be available on the CTO-as-a-Service platform from today.

sections.label: Productivity Solutions Grant savings
sections.summary: Between 2018 and 2023, digital solutions under the Productivity Solutions Grant brought nearly 50% cost savings to SMEs on average.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Between 2018 and 2023, digital solutions under the Productivity Solutions Grant brought nearly 50% cost savings to SMEs on average.

sections.label: Digital access support schemes
sections.summary: DigitalAccess@Home has supported over 20,000 low-income households since 2023, and Mobile Access for Seniors over 15,000 packages since 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: DigitalAccess@Home has supported over 20,000 low-income households with subsidised broadband access, a laptop or tablet, or both broadband and a computing device since 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The Mobile Access for Seniors scheme has also supported low-income seniors with over 15,000 packages of subsidised smartphones and mobile plans, or mobile plans only, since 2020.

sections.label: GovTech updating Digital Service Standards
sections.summary: GovTech will do more to support agencies, updating the Digital Service Standards this year to guide agencies in designing user-friendly digital services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: GovTech will do more to support agencies in this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: This year, we are updating the Digital Service Standards (DSS) which guide agencies in designing user-friendly digital services.

sections.label: MDDI digital services workgroup
sections.summary: MDDI will launch a workgroup with public, private and people sector partners to co-create and co-deliver more user-friendly digital services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: MDDI will launch a workgroup with partners from the public, private and people sectors to co-create and co-deliver initiatives to develop digital services that are more user-friendly.

sections.label: Singaporeans basic digital skills
sections.summary: Two in three Singaporeans have basic digital skills and can do day-to-day online tasks like buying, searching and contactless payments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Two in three Singaporeans have basic digital skills and are able to carry out day-to-day tasks online, such as buying products and services, searching for information and making contactless payments using a smartphone.

sections.label: SDO senior training and DSL
sections.summary: SDO has trained over 370,000 seniors since 2020, and IMDA will enhance the DSL framework with Gen AI content.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Since 2020, SDO has trained more than 370,000 seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Ninety-six percent of seniors communicate online as of 2023, up from 87% in 2017.

sentences.text: In MDDI's case, we conduct regular polls to gauge the public's awareness of scams as well as the quality of mainstream and online media and the public's news consumption habits.

sections.label: Scam SMS and call blocking
sections.summary: In 2023 IMDA implemented the full SMS sender ID registry regime, scam SMS cases fell 70%, and in 2024 117 million potential scam calls and 50 million potential scam SMSes were blocked.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Maybe to give the Member some sense of the usefulness of these efforts, in 2023, IMDA implemented the full SMS sender ID registry regime and non-registered SMSes are labelled as "likely scams".

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Cases of scam SMSes fell by 70% in the first three months of the regime's introduction and thereafter, it has remained low.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In 2024, 117 million potential scam calls from overseas were blocked.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For SMSes, 50 million potential scam SMSes were successfully blocked.

sections.label: Google enhanced fraud protection feature
sections.summary: The enhanced fraud protection feature with Google is turned on by default in Singapore and has blocked 1.6 million attempts to install potentially malicious apps across nearly 400,000 devices.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I mentioned briefly in my earlier speech how we are working with Google for the enhanced fraud protection feature.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This feature is turned on in Singapore by default and it has successfully blocked 1.6 million attempts to install potentially malicious apps across nearly 400,000 devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha

sections.label: SPH Media Trust KPIs
sections.summary: Reach was a KPI when SPH Media Trust funding was discussed, and trust and public satisfaction will now also be tracked as KPIs.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: When funding was discussed in support of SPH Media Trust at the time, reach was one of the important KPIs.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Over time, we also considered that engagement is important, is actually one of them, but in addition to that, we now think that trust as well as public satisfaction are just as important, so we will look to including them as part of the KPIs that we track for SPH Media Trust.

sections.label: NLB ChatBook safeguards
sections.summary: NLB's Gen AI-powered ChatBook featuring S Rajaratnam used a measured approach with controlled datasets, copyright permissions and extensive testing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: An example is the NLB's interactive ChatBook featuring S Rajaratnam, which was powered by Gen AI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, what NLB does is that it takes a measured approach to developing such prototypes and implements safeguards, such as using controlled datasets, securing copyrights and permissions from authors and creators to use their works, and carrying out extensive testing.

sections.label: MDDI survey coordination

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: In respect of the surveys, just to clarify, MDDI does not coordinate all surveys that are done by the Government because each Government agency will have to look at that individually.

sections.label: Withdrawing amendment and suspending Sitting

sentences.text: Can I invite Ms Tin Pei Ling, if you would like to withdraw the amendment?

sentences.text: It is, indeed, a complex amount of work that has to be put in in order to position us well in the digital realm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
